title: From a worry to a data question, safely
course_title: Data Literacy: Spreadsheets, Charts and Business Metrics

say: From a worry to a data question, safely.
This is the video for module 1 of Data Literacy.
Data is simply recorded facts. The bottles of zobo you sold on Saturday, or the date a member paid her contribution.
When facts are written down in an organised way, you can count them, compare them and learn from them.

say: Data literacy means you can look at a sales record or a chart and ask: what does this really show, is it accurate, and what should I do? It does not need advanced mathematics.

say: Numbers, like bottles sold or amount paid, can be added and averaged.

panel.heading: Four kinds of data
items: Numbers: amounts you can add or average
Categories: labels like cash, transfer, POS
Dates and times: when something happened
Free text: words people write or say

say: Categories can only be counted. A member ID like 0457 is a label, so it makes no sense to add member IDs together.

say: For example, Amaka sells chilled zobo near a bus park in Ibadan, and often throws away unsold bottles. Business is slow is a worry. A good question names what you measure and when.

panel.heading: Which day needs extra zobo?
items: Ask: how many bottles do I sell each day?
Collect: a tally every evening
Organise: add up the week, 138 bottles
Analyse: average about 19.7 a day
Decide: make more Friday and Saturday
panel.rule: Start with a clear question, not a spreadsheet.

say: She writes a tally each evening for one week: 18, 15, 17, 16, then 26 on Friday, 34 on Saturday and 12 on Sunday. That is 138 bottles.

say: 138 divided by 7 is about 19.7 bottles a day. Friday and Saturday are well above that, and Sunday is well below.

say: So she makes about 30 on Friday, 35 on Saturday and only 12 on Sunday.
But one week can be unusual because of rain or a holiday, so she keeps recording for three more weeks before any big change.

say: For example, Halima runs a provisions kiosk in Kaduna. Seven customers spend between 1,500 and 3,500 naira, plus one caterer who spends 20,000.
The mean adds everything and divides by 7. That gives about 4,929 naira, but only one customer spent more than that.

panel.heading: What does a typical customer spend?

cards.d: Add all 7 amounts, 34,500 naira, and divide by 7. One bulk buyer pulls it up.
Sort the amounts and take the middle one. This is the typical customer.
The amount that appears most often. Range: 20,000 minus 1,500 is ₦18,500.

say: The median is the middle value once they are sorted: 2,500 naira. That is the better answer, because one bulk buyer pulled the mean far upwards.

say: Use the mean when the values are fairly similar.

panel.heading: Mean or median?
right: One or two values are extreme

say: When one or two values are extreme, as with incomes, prices and rents, report the median.

right: One or two values are extreme

say: A percentage compares a part with a whole: part divided by whole, times 100. Percentage change is new minus old, divided by old, times 100.

card.title: Did sales really grow?
card.note: Always divide by the old value.

say: Sales were 250,000 naira in August and 300,000 in September. The change is 50,000 divided by 250,000, times 100. That is 20% growth.
The common mistake is dividing by the new value. That gives about 16.7%, which is wrong.

card.title: Did sales really grow?
card.note: Always divide by the old value.

say: Google Sheets is free, works on your phone and saves automatically to Google Drive, so a lost phone does not mean lost records.
Protect it. Use a long password phrase and turn on 2-Step Verification. Share as Viewer, and give Editor only to people who truly need it.

panel.heading: Protecting your Google Sheets
items: A long, unique password phrase
2-Step Verification turned on
Share as Viewer by default
No Anyone with the link for money records
Version history to undo mistakes

say: Personal data is a responsibility under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. For example, Fatima is treasurer of a 25-member savings group in Kano. She uses member codes, and keeps the names list in a separate file.

panel.heading: Fatima's safe contribution register
items: Member codes M01 to M25, not full names
Code list kept in a separate private file
Members can view; one person can edit
Payment proof sent privately, not in the group

say: Members can view and confirm their own entries, and payment screenshots no longer appear in a group chat.
And never share your OTP, BVN or banking PIN with anyone, even someone who says they are from your bank.

say: To remember. Start with a sharp question. Know your data types. Choose mean or median with care. Divide by the old value. And keep other people's data safe.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Question, collect, organise, analyse, decide
Numbers add up; categories are only counted
Extreme values? Report the median
Percentage change: new minus old, divided by old
Collect only the personal data you need
